coverage_gaps: The House Committee on Ethics archive and home page showed no new listed publication after the August 28 statement regarding House Reports 119-693 and 119-694. The Joseph/Roos contempt recommendation was adopted June 10, concerns non-congressional subjects without documented qualifying affiliation, and was already quarantined in the prior A03 artifact.

The Senate Select Committee on Ethics press-release archive showed no release newer than August 21, 2024; its public news page states that public activity is limited to annual reports, press releases, and public letters, with no in-window member-specific action located.

The Office of Congressional Conduct reports page returned 403 Forbidden through the web fetcher. The latest accessible reporting in prior scans remained the Second Quarter 2026 report dated July 23, 2026; this access limit prevents a claim of exhaustive OCC coverage.

Congress.gov was blocked by robots.txt. GovInfo Congressional Record collection and help/index pages were reviewed, and House Clerk member and vote pages were checked; no in-window ethics, misconduct, censure, resignation, removal, suspension, or related disciplinary action involving a qualifying subject was identified.

The DOJ all-news page listed August 28 releases involving unrelated defendants and no covered congressional member, leadership figure, or senior congressional staffer. The DOJ August 25 threat case involved an unnamed congressman as a victim, not a covered subject; it was not emitted or handed off.

AP, Axios, Washington Post, Roll Call, NOTUS, WUNC, New Jersey Globe, WLT Report, and other date-oriented searches surfaced only older Edwards, Miller, Mills, Bresnahan, and Gomez matters, or matters involving Democratic subjects and non-congressional persons. Those were excluded or deduplicated under the explicit-affiliation, procedural-status, and agent-lane rules.

This is a scoped negative scan rather than proof that no unindexed event exists; some congressional, judicial, and local-news indexes lack reliable date filtering through the available fetcher. Federal judicial and DOJ matters remain routed to A04 when they concern an in-scope qualifying subject.
